record.paper_title: A common approach to three open problems in number theory
record.original_question: Determine all positive-integer solutions (x, y) to x(x + 1) = y!. In particular, are the only such solutions (1, 2) and (2, 3)?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3. Hypothesis 3 implies that if the equation x1(x1 + 1) = x2! has at most finitely many solutions in positive integers x1 and x2, then each such solution (x1, x2) belongs to the set {(1, 2), (2, 3)}.
The question of solving the equation x(x + 1) = y! was posed by P. Erdos, see [1].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Determine all pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfying the Diophantine equation
    x(x + 1) = y!,
where y! denotes the factorial 1·2·3···y. Two solutions are immediate: (x, y) = (1, 2), since 1·2 = 2!, and (x, y) = (2, 3), since 2·3 = 3!. Prove or disprove that these are the only positive-integer solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: The equation x(x+1) = y!, posed by Erdős, remains an open Diophantine problem. While it is widely believed that (1,2) and (2,3) are the only positive integer solutions, no proof is known. Recent work by Terence Tao (2026) studies the anatomy of products of consecutive integers, motivated in part by this Erdős equation, but does not resolve the equation itself.

status_evidence.title: Products of consecutive integers with unusual anatomy
status_evidence.snippet: Questions of Erdős and Graham initially motivated by the study of the Diophantine factorial equation x(x+1) = y!, where x and y are positive integers.
status_evidence.claim: The equation x(x+1)=y! is referenced as a motivating open Diophantine problem of Erdős, with no known full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Erdős Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Database of Erdős problems including those concerning products of consecutive integers and factorials.
status_evidence.claim: The Erdős equation x(x+1)=y! is listed among Erdős's problems and is not marked as solved.
